schema_notes.fix_confidence: auto=mechanical fix always same, suggest=AI generates fix, human=judgment required
schema_notes.context_required: optional — extra context daemon checks before firing

footguns.title: Stale closure in useEffect
footguns.observation: This useEffect reads a variable but it's not in the dependency array — it'll silently use the stale value from the first render, not the current one.
footguns.agent_prompt: Fix the useEffect dependency array in {file} at line {line}. Add all variables referenced inside the effect. Don't change the effect logic.

detect_pattern.description: useEffect with non-empty body referencing identifiers not in dependency array

footguns.title: Object or array literal in dependency array causes infinite loop
footguns.observation: There's an object or array literal in this dependency array. It creates a new reference on every render — this effect will run on every render, effectively an infinite loop.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, move the object/array outside the component or wrap it in useMemo. Don't change the effect logic.

footguns.title: Array index as React key
footguns.observation: Using array index as key works until the list reorders or filters — then React reconciles the wrong elements, causing subtle state bugs and missed animations.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace the index key with a stable unique identifier from the data. Don't change anything else.

footguns.title: Direct state mutation
footguns.observation: This mutates state directly — React won't detect the change and the component won't re-render. State must be replaced, not mutated.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace the direct mutation with a new object/array using spread or Array methods. Pass the new value to the setter.

detect_pattern.description: state variable from useState assigned to or mutated directly without setter

footguns.title: useEffect with subscription or timer but no cleanup
footguns.observation: This effect sets up a subscription or timer but never cleans it up — it keeps running after the component unmounts, causing memory leaks.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add a return cleanup function to the useEffect that cancels the interval or removes the listener.

detect_pattern.description: useEffect containing setInterval/addEventListener/subscribe with no return function

footguns.title: No error boundary around async data components
footguns.observation: Components that fetch data have no error boundary — a single runtime error in a child will unmount the entire tree and show a blank screen.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file}, wrap the data-fetching component tree with an ErrorBoundary component. Show a meaningful fallback UI on error.

detect_pattern.description: component using useEffect for data fetch with no surrounding error boundary in tree

footguns.title: v-for without :key
footguns.observation: v-for without a :key causes Vue to reuse DOM elements incorrectly when the list updates — leading to wrong state being shown in the wrong items.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add :key with a stable unique identifier to the v-for directive. Don't use the loop index.

footguns.title: Adding new property to reactive object directly (Vue 2)
footguns.observation: Vue 2 can't detect property additions on reactive objects — this change won't trigger re-renders. Use Vue.set() or replace the whole object.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace direct property assignment with Vue.set(object, property, value) or replace the entire object with a spread.
footguns.context_required: vue 2 project (check package.json for vue version < 3)

detect_pattern.description: new property assigned directly on this.data or reactive() object in Vue 2 project

footguns.title: Next.js API route with no authentication check
footguns.observation: This API route has no authentication check — it's publicly accessible to anyone who knows the URL.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add an auth check at the top of the handler. Verify the session or token before processing the request. Return 401 if not authenticated.
footguns.context_required: app has auth system — check for next-auth, clerk, or similar in package.json

detect_pattern.description: pages/api or app/api route handler with no session/token check near the top

footguns.title: Server-side env variable used in client component
footguns.observation: A server-side environment variable (without NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix) is used in a client component — it will be bundled and exposed in the browser.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, either prefix the variable with NEXT_PUBLIC_ if it's safe to expose, or move this logic to a server component or API route.

detect_pattern.description: process.env.VARIABLE (without NEXT_PUBLIC_) in a 'use client' component or pages/ file

footguns.title: Type cast to any bypasses all type safety
footguns.observation: Casting to any silences TypeScript completely for this value — any type error downstream will be a runtime surprise instead of a compile-time catch.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace the 'as any' cast with the correct type or an unknown cast with a type guard. Don't suppress the error — fix the type.

footguns.title: Non-null assertion on value that can be null
footguns.observation: The ! operator tells TypeScript to trust you that this value is never null — but if it ever is, you get a runtime crash with no type warning.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace the ! assertion with a proper null check or optional chaining (?.). Handle the null case explicitly.

footguns.title: Unhandled promise rejection
footguns.observation: This promise has no error handling — an unhandled rejection crashes the process in Node 15+ or silently swallows the error in older versions.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add try/catch around the await or a .catch() on the promise. Handle or rethrow the error.

detect_pattern.description: await or .then() with no surrounding try/catch and no .catch()

footguns.title: Synchronous operation blocking event loop
footguns.observation: This synchronous operation runs on the event loop thread — it blocks every other request while it runs. In production this tanks throughput under any load.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace with the async equivalent or move the heavy computation to a worker thread. Don't change the surrounding logic.

footguns.title: Prototype pollution via unsafe object merge
footguns.observation: Merging user-controlled objects without sanitising __proto__ or constructor keys allows prototype pollution — attackers can inject properties onto every object in the process.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, sanitise the input to strip __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys before merging.

detect_pattern.description: recursive merge or Object.assign with user-controlled input (req.body) as source

footguns.title: typeof null === 'object' — the classic JavaScript bug
footguns.observation: typeof null returns 'object' — this is a 20-year-old JavaScript bug that never got fixed. Checking typeof x === 'object' without a null check will pass for null.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add an explicit null check: typeof x === 'object' && x !== null.

footguns.title: trust proxy set to true — IP spoofing risk
footguns.observation: Setting trust proxy to true trusts all proxy headers unconditionally — an attacker can spoof their IP by setting X-Forwarded-For to anything.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace 'trust proxy', true with 'trust proxy', 1 (or the correct hop count for your proxy setup).

footguns.title: No error handling middleware
footguns.observation: This Express app has no error handling middleware — unhandled errors return a full stack trace to the client in development and crash silently in production.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file}, add error handling middleware with 4 arguments (err, req, res, next) as the last middleware. Return a sanitised error response.

detect_pattern.description: express app file with no 4-argument middleware registered

footguns.title: Server-side secret exposed in client bundle
footguns.observation: This environment variable is being used in client-side code — it will be bundled and shipped to every browser. If it's a secret key or token it's now public.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, move this logic to the server side or replace the secret with a public-safe value.

detect_pattern.description: process.env access in client-side file (no NEXT_PUBLIC_ or VITE_ prefix)

footguns.title: SQL injection via string interpolation
footguns.observation: This SQL query is built with string interpolation — any user-controlled input can break out of the query and execute arbitrary SQL.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace string interpolation with parameterised queries. Pass user values as parameters, never inline.

detect_pattern.description: string template or concatenation containing req.body/req.params/req.query inside SQL keyword context

footguns.title: Auth endpoint with no rate limiting
footguns.observation: This auth endpoint has no rate limiting — it's open to credential stuffing and brute force attacks.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add rate limiting middleware. Limit to 5-10 attempts per IP per 15 minutes.
footguns.context_required: route path contains login, signin, auth, password-reset

detect_pattern.description: POST handler with auth-related path and no rate limiting middleware

footguns.title: Goroutine leak — no exit condition
footguns.observation: This goroutine has no way to exit — it leaks memory for the lifetime of the process. Under load these accumulate fast.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add a context or done channel to this goroutine so it can exit cleanly. Select on it inside the goroutine.

detect_pattern.description: go func() with no context parameter and no done channel or guaranteed return

footguns.title: Loop variable captured by goroutine closure (pre-Go 1.22)
footguns.observation: This goroutine closes over the loop variable — by the time it runs, the loop has finished and the variable holds the last value, not the intended one. Fixed in Go 1.22 but older codebases still have this.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, shadow the loop variable before passing it to the goroutine: v := v before the go func(). Or upgrade to Go 1.22.

detect_pattern.description: for loop variable referenced inside go func() or goroutine closure without shadowing

footguns.title: Write to nil map causes panic
footguns.observation: Writing to a nil map panics at runtime — the map needs to be initialised with make() before any key is set.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, initialise the map with make(map[KeyType]ValueType) before writing to it.

detect_pattern.description: map variable declared with var (nil) and written to without make()

footguns.title: defer inside a loop — cleanup deferred until function returns
footguns.observation: defer inside a loop doesn't run until the function returns — not at the end of each iteration. Files and connections stay open for the entire loop.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, extract the loop body into a separate function with the defer inside it, or call cleanup explicitly at each iteration.

detect_pattern.description: defer statement inside for loop body

footguns.title: Error return value explicitly discarded
footguns.observation: This explicitly discards an error return. Even if it seems unimportant, silently ignoring errors makes debugging production failures significantly harder.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, handle the error instead of discarding it. At minimum log it. If it's safe to ignore, add a comment explaining why.

footguns.title: context.Background() in HTTP handler ignores cancellation
footguns.observation: Creating a new background context inside a handler ignores the request's cancellation signal — if the client disconnects, downstream operations keep running.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace context.Background() with r.Context() to propagate request cancellation.
footguns.context_required: inside an http.Handler or gin/echo handler function

footguns.title: FROM latest — non-deterministic builds
footguns.observation: Using :latest means your builds are non-deterministic — the base image changes between builds and breaks things in ways that are very hard to debug in production.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, pin the base image to a specific version tag or SHA digest.

footguns.title: Container runs as root by default
footguns.observation: Containers that don't specify a USER instruction run as root — if the container is compromised, the attacker has root access to everything it can reach.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file}, add a USER instruction before the final CMD or ENTRYPOINT. Create a non-root user with useradd if needed.

detect_pattern.description: Dockerfile with no USER instruction before CMD or ENTRYPOINT

footguns.title: Secret or credential in Dockerfile layer
footguns.observation: Secrets in Dockerfile ARG or ENV instructions are baked into image layers — even if you unset them later they're recoverable from the layer history.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, remove the secret from the Dockerfile. Use Docker BuildKit secrets (--mount=type=secret) or pass them at runtime via environment.

footguns.title: Terraform state file committed to repository
footguns.observation: Terraform state files contain plaintext secrets, resource IDs, and full infrastructure details. Committing them exposes your entire infrastructure.
footguns.agent_prompt: Add terraform.tfstate and terraform.tfstate.backup to .gitignore immediately. Configure a remote backend (S3, GCS, Terraform Cloud) for state storage.

footguns.title: Container with no resource limits
footguns.observation: Containers without resource limits can consume unbounded CPU and memory — one misbehaving pod can starve the entire node.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file}, add resources.requests and resources.limits to the container spec. Start with modest values based on typical usage.

detect_pattern.description: Kubernetes Deployment or Pod spec YAML with containers section but no resources.limits

footguns.title: Secret value echoed in workflow logs
footguns.observation: This workflow step prints a secret to the log — GitHub masks known secrets but only if they're declared as secrets. Derived or modified secret values are not masked.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, remove the echo/print of the secret value. If you need to debug, use a step summary instead of stdout.

detect_pattern.description: echo or run step printing ${{ secrets.* }} value directly

footguns.title: Third-party action without pinned SHA
footguns.observation: Using a third-party action pinned to a tag (v1, v2) means the action owner can push malicious code to that tag and it will run in your pipeline. Pin to a full commit SHA instead.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace the tag reference with the full commit SHA of that tag. Check the action's releases page.

footguns.title: Hardcoded secret, key, or token in source
footguns.observation: There's what looks like a hardcoded secret in this file. Even in private repositories this is a risk — git history is permanent and repository access changes.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, move this value to an environment variable or secret manager. Replace the literal with a lookup.

detect_pattern.description: string literal matching common secret patterns: high entropy, API key format, private key header

footguns.title: JWT verification without explicit algorithm allowlist
footguns.observation: Not specifying allowed algorithms in JWT verification allows the 'none' algorithm attack — an attacker can forge tokens by removing the signature entirely.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add an explicit algorithms allowlist to the JWT verify call. Never allow 'none'. Specify only the algorithms you actually use.

detect_pattern.description: jwt.verify() or equivalent called without algorithms option

footguns.title: State-changing endpoint with no CSRF protection
footguns.observation: This state-changing endpoint has no CSRF protection — a malicious site can trick an authenticated user's browser into making requests to it.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add CSRF token validation middleware to this route. Or set SameSite=Strict on the session cookie.
footguns.context_required: uses cookie-based auth (not JWT in header)

detect_pattern.description: POST/PUT/DELETE handler in cookie-auth app with no csrf middleware

footguns.title: Non-cryptographic RNG for security-sensitive values
footguns.observation: Math.random() / rand() is predictable and must never be used for tokens, session IDs, or passwords.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace with crypto.randomBytes() (Node), secrets.token_hex() (Python), or crypto/rand (Go).
footguns.context_required: used in auth, token generation, or password reset context

detect_pattern.description: Math.random() or rand() in token/session/password generation context

footguns.title: User input used without validation
footguns.observation: User input is being used directly without validation — depending on context this could be injection, path traversal, or command injection.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, validate and sanitise the input before using it. Use an allowlist — define what's valid, reject everything else.

detect_pattern.description: req.body/req.params/req.query used directly in file path, command, or DB context

footguns.title: Data leakage — preprocessing before train/test split
footguns.observation: Fitting the preprocessor on the full dataset before splitting leaks test data into training — your evaluation metrics are unreliable and the model's real-world performance is unknown.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, fit the preprocessor only on training data. Use a Pipeline to ensure transforms are applied correctly to both sets.

detect_pattern.description: fit_transform() or fit() called on full dataset before train_test_split()

footguns.title: Accuracy on imbalanced dataset is misleading
footguns.observation: Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced datasets — a model predicting only the majority class can score 95%+ accuracy while being completely useless.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace or supplement accuracy with F1, precision, recall, or AUC-ROC depending on your use case.

detect_pattern.description: accuracy_score used as only metric on dataset with class distribution > 80/20

footguns.title: Mutable default argument — shared across all calls
footguns.observation: Mutable default arguments are shared across all calls — the object is created once when the function is defined, not each time it's called. Mutations persist between calls.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace the mutable default with None and initialise it inside the function body: if x is None: x = []

footguns.title: datetime.now() as default argument — evaluated once at module load
footguns.observation: Default arguments are evaluated once when the function is defined — datetime.now() as a default gives the same timestamp forever, not the current time when called.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace datetime.now() with None as the default and call datetime.now() inside the function body.

footguns.title: Bare except catches SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt
footguns.observation: A bare except catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit — the program can't be stopped with Ctrl+C and deployment scripts can't terminate it cleanly.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace the bare except with specific exception types. If you must catch broadly, use except Exception as e: and log the error.

footguns.title: Chained assignment modifies a copy — change disappears silently
footguns.observation: Chained indexing on the left side of an assignment modifies a copy, not the original DataFrame — the change silently disappears.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace chained assignment with .loc[mask, col] = value to modify the original DataFrame directly.

footguns.title: No random seed — non-reproducible experiment results
footguns.observation: Without a fixed seed, results differ between runs — experiments aren't reproducible and results can't be compared reliably.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, set random_state=42 on the model and train_test_split calls. Add numpy.random.seed() at the top of the script.

detect_pattern.description: model instantiation or train_test_split with no random_state parameter

footguns.title: model.eval() not called before inference
footguns.observation: Without model.eval(), dropout and batch normalisation layers behave differently at inference than at training — predictions will be inconsistent and slightly wrong.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, call model.eval() before the inference block and wrap it in torch.no_grad(): for efficiency.

detect_pattern.description: model called for inference/prediction without preceding model.eval()

footguns.title: Gradients not zeroed before backward pass
footguns.observation: PyTorch accumulates gradients by default — not calling optimizer.zero_grad() before each backward pass means gradients from previous batches accumulate, corrupting training.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add optimizer.zero_grad() before loss.backward() in the training loop.

detect_pattern.description: loss.backward() in training loop without preceding optimizer.zero_grad()

footguns.title: Notebook cells executed out of order
footguns.observation: Cell execution numbers show this notebook has been run out of order — results may not be reproducible by running top-to-bottom, and shared notebooks will confuse collaborators.
footguns.note: Restart kernel and run all cells to verify top-to-bottom reproducibility.

detect_pattern.description: Jupyter notebook with non-sequential execution_count values in cell metadata

footguns.title: FlatList without keyExtractor
footguns.observation: FlatList without keyExtractor falls back to the item's index — causing incorrect recycling of list items when the list updates, producing visual glitches.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add a keyExtractor prop that returns a stable unique string from each item. Use the item's ID, not its index.

detect_pattern.description: FlatList component without keyExtractor prop

footguns.title: Sensitive data in AsyncStorage — unencrypted
footguns.observation: AsyncStorage is unencrypted and accessible on rooted/jailbroken devices. Tokens and credentials belong in the secure keychain.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace AsyncStorage with react-native-keychain or expo-secure-store for this sensitive value.
footguns.context_required: value key or stored value contains: token, password, secret, key, auth

footguns.title: Large object crossing React Native bridge
footguns.observation: Passing large objects across the JS-native bridge is expensive — each crossing serialises and deserialises the entire object. Large payloads here cause janky UI.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, minimise the data crossing the bridge. Pass only the fields needed. Move heavy computation to the native side or use a shared buffer.

detect_pattern.description: NativeModule call or native event with large object payload

footguns.title: Heavy computation on JS thread causing frame drops
footguns.observation: Heavy synchronous JS on the main thread blocks UI rendering — anything over ~16ms causes visible frame drops on device.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, move this computation to InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions() or a background task.

detect_pattern.description: heavy array operation or synchronous computation inside render or event handler

footguns.title: Force unwrapping optional — will crash if nil
footguns.observation: Force unwrapping with ! crashes the app if the value is nil. This is one of the most common causes of Swift app crashes in production.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace force unwrap with guard let, if let, or the nil coalescing operator ??. Handle the nil case explicitly.

footguns.title: Strong reference cycle in closure — memory leak
footguns.observation: This closure captures self strongly — if self also holds a reference to this closure, neither will be deallocated. Common pattern in delegates and completion handlers.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, add [weak self] or [unowned self] to the closure capture list. Guard against nil if using weak.

detect_pattern.description: closure that captures self without [weak self] or [unowned self]

footguns.title: Coroutine scope not tied to lifecycle — memory leak
footguns.observation: Launching coroutines in GlobalScope or a custom scope not tied to the lifecycle means they keep running after the Activity or Fragment is destroyed.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, replace GlobalScope.launch with lifecycleScope.launch or viewModelScope.launch so coroutines cancel with the lifecycle.

footguns.title: Permission used without privacy description in Info.plist
footguns.observation: iOS crashes the app at runtime if a permission is requested without a usage description string in Info.plist. App Store review will also reject the build.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {repo}/ios/Info.plist, add the missing NSUsageDescription key with a clear user-facing explanation of why the app needs this permission.

detect_pattern.description: camera/microphone/location/contacts API used without corresponding NSUsageDescription in Info.plist

footguns.title: Cleartext HTTP traffic allowed globally
footguns.observation: Allowing cleartext HTTP traffic globally exposes users to MITM attacks. Android 9+ blocks it by default for good reason.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file}, remove android:usesCleartextTraffic=true and update HTTP URLs to HTTPS. If a specific domain needs HTTP, scope it in a network security config.

footguns.title: Debug mode enabled in production config
footguns.observation: Debug mode in production can leak stack traces, internal paths, environment variables, and sensitive data in error responses.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, set DEBUG=false and log level to warn or error in production. Guard verbose logging behind environment checks.

footguns.title: Sensitive user data in log statements
footguns.observation: This log statement may be printing sensitive user data — logs are stored, aggregated, and accessed by many people and systems.
footguns.agent_prompt: In {file} at line {line}, remove or redact the sensitive fields. Log the shape of the data, not the values.
footguns.context_required: logged variable name contains: password, token, secret, key, email, credit_card

detect_pattern.description: console.log/print/logger containing variable with sensitive-looking name

footguns.title: TODO or FIXME in security-critical code
footguns.observation: There's an unresolved TODO in a security-critical path. These tend to stay unresolved much longer than intended and often represent known weaknesses.
footguns.note: No agent prompt — this requires a human decision about what the TODO means.
footguns.context_required: within 5 lines of auth check, payment processing, or permission validation

detect_pattern.description: TODO or FIXME comment near auth/payments/permission code
